A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heavy metal concentrations in squash fruits were below the maximum permissible levels and that the use of MSS and MSS-YW as organic mulch in the field did not pose a threat to human health.
the use of municipal sewage sludge in soil did not result in heavy metal concentrations that exceeded the limits set in U.S. EPA guidelines for land application of sewage sludge.
the use of MSS and MSS-YW as soil amendment in the study did not increase heavy metal concentrations in summer squash fruits to levels that would be considered harmful for human health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of compost made from MSS and mixed with yard waste is a safe practice for growing vegetables in urban areas.
the use of MSS in the soil did not increase the concentration of heavy metals in the edible portion of the squash fruits at harvest.
the use of MSS-YW and composted MSS in land farming does not pose any threat of Cd, Ni, Pb, and Zn bioaccumulation in squash fruit.
